ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a coupled-coil circuit driven by current source i(t). On the left side are the primary-side current source and primary coil, and on the right side is the secondary coil, whose terminals are labeled A and B. The A-B end is connected to a branch with switch S; when S is closed, the 30 Ω resistor is connected between A and B and becomes the secondary-side load. In the figure, the secondary-side inductance is taken as L2 = 1 H, and the mutual inductance is taken as M = 0.8 H. Reasoning calculation: The problem changes the current to i(t)=10 sin(100πt) A, so using peak phasors, take I1,pk = 10 A, and angular frequency ω = 100π rad/s. The magnitude of the secondary-side induced voltage peak phasor is |jωMI1| = ωMI1 = 100π × 0.8 × 10 = 800π V. The secondary-side self-inductance impedance is jωL2 = j100π Ω, and the load is R = 30 Ω. When S is closed, the A-B terminal peak voltage by voltage division is |V_AB,pk| = |jωMI1 · R/(R + jωL2)| = 800π × 30 / sqrt(30^2 + (100π)^2) ≈ 238.9 V, taken as approximately 240 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a current-source-driven coupled-coil circuit whose secondary terminal pair A-B is shunted by the 30 Ω resistor when S is closed. Convert the changed current waveform from the question to phasor peak form, I1 = 10 at angular frequency 100π rad/s. From the image use L2 = 1 H and M = 0.8 H. Model the secondary as an induced sinusoidal voltage jωMI1 in series with jωL2 feeding R = 30 Ω. Compute the peak terminal/load voltage by the phasor voltage divider: V_AB,pk = |jωMI1 · R/(R + jωL2)| ≈ 240 V.
